title: A Unified Framework for Uniform-Price Resource Allocation Mechanisms
claim: Across pricing-parameter settings, learning dynamics in the mechanism converge to low exploitability, with differences driven by the mechanism's tuning parameter.
layout: 3 panels in a row, shared axes, beta value as large label below each
description: Three side-by-side line plots, each titled 'Hedge in α-Proportional Mechanism'. Every panel plots exploitability (log scale, about -2 down to -5) against iteration (0 to 10000). Each has four noisy dotted curves for alpha = 0.1 (blue), 0.25 (orange), 0.5 (green) and 1 (red). All curves start high and decay quickly, then slowly, toward about -5. Large LaTeX labels below the panels give beta = 1, 0.75 and 0.5. At beta = 1 the curves overlap, and orange dips lowest. As beta decreases, alpha = 0.1 (blue) separates and converges more slowly, while the other curves cluster together. The eye goes first to the decaying curves, then to the large beta labels.
caption: Exploitability under Hedge dynamics for different values of β.
abstract: Mechanisms for allocating a divisible resource among strategic agents have been widely studied. The prominent paradigm is the proportional (Kelly) mechanism, which elicits a scalar bid per agent, allocates the resource proportionally, and charges payments equal to the bids. Follow-up mechanisms improve social welfare, but sacrifice simplicity by introducing complex allocation rules or unintuitive payments. We introduce a unified framework for designing simple resource allocation mechanisms with proportional-style allocations and uniform pricing. Our framework yields a family of mechanisms that interpolate between the Kelly mechanism and the first-price auction. These mechanisms strictly improve upon Kelly's efficiency guarantees, even achieving full efficiency in equilibrium, while also providing revenue guarantees relative to the VCG mechanism.
